source.title: Differentiated Directional Intervention A Framework for Evading LLM Safety Alignment

record.file_problem: Full paper text and appendix are present. Some PDF extraction and formatting artifacts appear in equations and tables.
record.tranche_reason: The paper builds and evaluates an inference-time activation jailbreak using refusal and harm-related directions. It reports the attack's harmful-compliance outcomes, but does not test the listed fine-tuning, first-token, prefill/suffix/decoding, weight-localization, shallowness-cause, or safety-deepening claims.
record.gate_note: The paper reports harmful-compliance outcomes from its own activation intervention; those are recorded as findings about activation-based jailbreak efficacy, not as tests of the listed versions. It does not measure per-token KL, compliant-prefix effects, fine-tuning effects, or safety weights/ranks. Prior-work results mentioned in comparisons are not extracted as findings for those methods.
record.test_reason: The paper proposes and evaluates an inference-time activation-steering jailbreak (DBDI) built on harm-detection and refusal-execution directions. It reports only its own attack's ASR, harmfulness scores and ablations. It does not fine-tune models (V1/V2), measure per-token KL (V3), or test prefill, suffix or decoding attacks (V4). Activation directions are not weight or rank localization (V5), and it tests neither the cause of shallowness (V6) nor deepening defences (V7). The original Qi et al. fine-tuning paper is cited only as related work on parameter-modification attacks. The paper does not rely on the shallow-alignment finding, so cites_only/T6 fits better than the reader's uses_without_test/T4.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors claim safety comprises distinct harm-detection and refusal-execution directions. They conclude that a sequential, differentiated intervention on these directions (DBDI) effectively bypasses safety alignment, outperforming single-direction and prompt-based attacks.
record.recipe_differences: The paper uses inference-time activation extraction and intervention, not fine-tuning or token-position KL measurement.
record.method_sensitivity: Attack outcomes vary with model, benchmark, chat template, intervention layer, intervention order, sparsification threshold, and calibration sample count.

fits_no_version.finding: Steering on a sparse refusal-execution direction plus a harm-detection direction at one mid layer raises harmful compliance from near 0% to 80-98% ASR across four instruct models. The effect depends on layer, intervention order and ablation variant: layer 30 gives 0.19%, reversed order gives 2.11%, and single-direction variants give 1-20%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal in aligned LLMs can be bypassed by an inference-time activation intervention on separate harm-detection and refusal-execution directions at a mid layer. Its efficacy depends on layer, order and direction choice.

record.problems: The authors state that they use greedy decoding and therefore do not report standard deviations or statistical significance tests. The main reported ASR results use LlamaGuard-3-8B as an automated evaluator, while StrongREJECT uses its own evaluator. Results are reported for selected models and benchmarks; the paper does not provide uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: Within the 60-row limit, not all Table 4 metrics (HarmBench and StrongREJECT), the hyperparameter heatmap, and comparison results for other methods are included. Table 4 ASR ablations, Table 6 AdvBench calibration-size results, Table 7 layer results, Table 8 intervention-order results, Figure 3 sparsification results, and DBDI entries from Tables 2 and 3 are retained.

untested.parts: No harmful fine-tuning. Malicious fine-tuning is only discussed as prior work.
No per-token KL or position-wise analysis of aligned vs base models.
No prefilling, suffix or decoding attacks. GCG and other suffix numbers in Table 3 are cited from other works, not run as tests of V4.
No weight or rank localization. Sparse activation-neuron masks and layer choice concern activation directions, not parameters.
No analysis of data or objective causes of shallowness.

record.verdict_notes: Table 1 lists Llama-3.1-8B, Vicuna and Mistral, but no results for them appear. The appendix refers to the method as 'AHI' in places. ASR is judged by LlamaGuard-3-8B with greedy decoding and no uncertainty. Comparison numbers for other methods are taken from prior publications and are correctly not extracted as rows.

versions.untested_parts: Fine-tuning on harmful examples and refusal rates after such training.
Fine-tuning on benign data and resulting harmful-compliance rates.
Per-token KL divergence between aligned and base models across response positions.
Prefilling compliant response tokens, adversarial suffixes, and decoding changes. The paper instead evaluates internal activation intervention.
Whether a small set of model weights or ranks carries safety behaviour. Sparse activation-vector neurons are not a weight/rank localization test.
Whether training data or objective causes safety to be shallow in response-token positions.
Training to spread safety beyond early response tokens and testing whether that safety holds.

relation.reason: The paper cites harmful fine-tuning and parameter-pruning studies as related work, but neither tests their claim versions nor relies on those findings to implement DBDI.

tranche.reason: The results evaluate an inference-time activation attack and its ablations, without testing V1–V7. Sparsifying activation directions does not establish localization in model weights or ranks (V5); the cited shallow-alignment findings are not used as a tool.

source_check.notes: The official PDF's hash matches provenance; its title, authors and arXiv:2511.06852v4 date (24 November 2025) match the supplied snapshot, and its extracted text is identical, with no material version differences. All required images (pages 6, 7 and 11) were inspected successfully; visual evidence resolves extraction layout, with no stored-field errors found.
